answer_1.quote: We run experiments on three controlled text generation tasks -couplet completion in poetry, topic control in language generation, and formality change in machine translation
datasets: Fisher and CALLHOME Spanish-English Speech Translation Corpus
answer_1.outputs: Generated couplets, topic-controlled text, formal translations

answer_2.quote: Metrics. We consider four metrics. 1. Success, the fraction of couplet completions with the desired attribute a, as checked by F. This is the main metric. 2. Grammaticality, the probability of grammaticality given by a Roberta-based CoLA grammaticality model, averaged over all outputs. 3. Perplexity of the completion conditioned on the prefix. 4. Distinctness... Additionally, we adopt a notion of success which requires the model to generalize the bag W to the full topic... BLEU Score, using two of Salesky et al.'s fluent references per test example... Formality, the average probability that the model's outputs are formal...

answer_4.quote: Additionally, following the evaluation procedure of prior work such as, we run human evaluations via Amazon Mechanical Turk for FUDGE against each baseline, comparing topic control and fluency. For each pairwise comparison, we ask 3 workers to evaluate each of 420 paired outputs. Workers were asked to mark which generation is more on topic (first, second, both, or neither), and to rate each generation's fluency on a Likert scale from 1 to 5.
answer_4.guideline: Workers mark which generation is more on topic and rate fluency on a Likert scale.
